nonblocking_findings: PDF p.89 (printed 81): The text is clean. The Hebrew points are readable, with no clipping or overlap, and paragraph spacing is even. The rubric 'The Reader says half Kaddish.' is left-aligned. The speaker label חזן stays on the same row as its Kaddish line. The English instruction paragraph mixes Hebrew terms (תפלה, ואני תפלתי, האזינו, ארון הקדש, קדושה, אבינו מלכנו, קדיש תתקבל, קדיש יתום, עלינו) in the right order. The page links 31, 31 and 41 have boxes around them. The heading קריאת התורה למנחה של ראש השנה has a proper gap above and below it.

PDF p.89: The bold English label '(On Sabbath)' over the ואני תפלתי block, set between two short rules, is aligned to the right margin. Every other English rubric on these pages is aligned left. Its parentheses are in the right order and it is readable, so this is cosmetic. Check that the right alignment is intended for conditional labels.

PDF p.90 (printed 82): Footnote mark 98 sits between the first and second lines of the לוי paragraph, above the start of line 2 where the enlarged ה appears (הֲ לַיהוָה). It does not overlap line 1 and is legible. At this image resolution I could not confirm that it sits exactly over the enlarged letter rather than over the nearby word וּפְתַלְתֹּל.

PDF p.90: Footnote 98 ('ה' רבתי, והוא מלה לעצמה.') is on the same page as its mark, and the number is on the right, as Hebrew reading order requires. It is the only footnote in this range, so numbering order is consistent. The footnote separator rule is on the left margin while the footnote text is right-aligned. This is cosmetic.

PDF p.90: The סדר תשליך and שיר של יום headings have proper gaps around them. The English Tashlikh rubric is left-aligned and complete. The Hebrew-only Tashlikh and Psalm 24 (שיר של יום) text is set as one full-width column, with no columns or rows misaligned and no translation added.
PDF pp.90–91: The running head 'שיר של יום.' carries over onto the back-matter pages (Metadata/Legal on p.90, Contributor credits/Sources on p.91). This is common LaTeX behaviour and cosmetic.

PDF p.91 (printed 83): The contributor credits and source entry [1] are complete and readable. The long URL and identifier break cleanly over several lines inside their link boxes, with nothing clipped. Neither obsolete editorial note claiming coverage stops at 311 appears on any page in this range.

PDF p.92: This page has no running head or page number. The text on it is two disposal/genizah advisory bullets placed at the bottom of an otherwise blank page. It reads as a deliberate back-matter colophon placed at the bottom. The bullets are complete and not clipped.
The link borders in these renders look cyan/blue rather than red. They are consistent across page-reference and URL links and are clearly hyperref borders, not debug highlighting.
limitations: I judged only the four assigned page images (PDF pp.89–92, printed 81–83 plus an unnumbered final page) and the manifest. I did not reread the source or check other page ranges.
The priestly blessing, Musaf closing, the early English-only peace blessing and the thirty-blast instruction do not appear in this range, so I could not check them visually here.
Exact horizontal placement of interlinear mark 98 relative to the enlarged ה can only be estimated at this raster resolution.
The manifest's source_batch_pages (84–89) overlap this range only at PDF p.89. I could not check pp.84–88 from these images.
